```{r setup}
library(meraconstraints)
library(glue)
```


## Minimal example


```{r}
d1 <- initialize_graph(graph_from_literal(V1 -+ V2, V2 -+ V3, V3 -+ V4, U1 -+ V1:V3, U2 -+ V2:V4))
plot(d1)
```

This has no conditional independences: 
```{r}
dag_list_independences(d1)
```

It does however have a nontrivial inequality constraint that we can find. 

```{r}
d1r <- dag_transform_canonical_partition(d1) |> 
    dag_transform_response_functions()
```

In this example we want q(V1, V2, V3) = p(V1, V2, V3) / p(V2 | V1)= p(V3 | V2, V1) p(V1)
examining ptabs, we see that it is linear in p(R_V1, R_V3) because the p(R_V2) cancels out when you divide. 

```{r}
ptabs <- dag_get_cf_tables(d1r, expand.grid(V1 = 0:1, V3 = 0:1, V2 = 0:1))
#dag_get_moebius_params(d1)
cf.form <- list(out = c("R_V1", "R_V3"), cond = NULL)
relation <- split(ptabs[, c("R_V1", "R_V3")], ptabs[, c("V1","V2", "V3")]) |> 
  lapply(\(pt) {
    unique(make_prob_names(cf.form, pt))
  })
prob.fancy <- split(ptabs, ptabs[, c("V1","V2", "V3")]) |> 
  sapply(\(pt) {
    unique(glue_data(pt, "p(V3 = {V3} | V2 = {V2}, V1 = {V1}) * p(V1 = {V1})"))
  })

hrepd1 <- cf_relations_to_hrep(prob.fancy, relation)
hrep_to_text(hrepd1$Hrep, prob.fancy)
```

We can see in the above that there are some obviously trivial constraints, we can remove these by identifying the sets of probabilities that sum to 1. 

```{r}
sets1 <- split(ptabs[, c("V1", "V2", "V3")], ptabs[, c("V2")]) |> 
  lapply(\(pt) {
    unique(glue_data(pt, "p(V3 = {V3} | V2 = {V2}, V1 = {V1}) * p(V1 = {V1})"))
  })

hrep_to_text(hrepd1$Hrep, prob.fancy, sets1, simplify = TRUE)
```
The first 2 elements here are the nontrivial inequalities but the second pair are problematic. Elements 3 and 4 both represent the same equality constraint (after some simple manipulation): 
$$
p(V_1 = 0 | V_2 = 0) = p(V_1 = 0 | V_2 = 1), 
$$
or in other words $V_1$ is independent of $V_2$, which is obviously not true given the DAG. This is a spurious independence that we know is coming. It is because the post-truncation distribution is obtained by the fixing operation on $V_2$, i.e., removing incoming arrows into $V_2$. That graph looks like this: 
```{r}
d1f <- initialize_graph(graph_from_literal(V2 -+ V3, U -+ V1:V3))
plot(d1f)

dag_list_independences(d1f)
```
from which we can clearly see the independence between $V_2$ and $V_1$. We just need to remove it from our "discovered" constraints. To do that, let's identify all ways of representing the independence in terms of the probabilities of the form $p(V_3, V_1 | V_2)$. 

Marginalize out $V_3$, sum terms where $V_3$ differs but $V_1, V_2$ are the same, subtract the same but where $V_2$ is the other value.
```{r}
pfd1 <- do.call(rbind, split(ptabs[, c("V1","V2", "V3")], ptabs[, c("V1","V2", "V3")]) |> 
  lapply(\(pt) {
    unique(pt)
  }))

M <- NULL

zeros <- c(1, 0, rep(0, length(prob.fancy)))
zeros[2 + which(with(pfd1, V1 == 0 & V2 == 0 & V3 %in% 0:1))] <- 1
zeros[2 + which(with(pfd1, V1 == 0 & V2 == 1 & V3 %in% 0:1))] <- -1
zeros[2] <- 0
M <- rbind(M, zeros)
zeros <- c(1, 0, rep(0, length(prob.fancy)))
zeros[2 + which(with(pfd1, V1 == 1 & V2 == 0 & V3 %in% 0:1))] <- 1
zeros[2 + which(with(pfd1, V1 == 1 & V2 == 1 & V3 %in% 0:1))] <- -1
zeros[2] <- 0
M <- rbind(M, zeros)

zeros <- c(1, 0, rep(0, length(prob.fancy)))
zeros[2 + which(with(pfd1, V1 == 0 & V2 == 0 & V3 %in% 0:1))] <- -1
zeros[2 + which(with(pfd1, V1 == 0 & V2 == 1 & V3 %in% 0:1))] <- 1
zeros[2] <- 0
M <- rbind(M, zeros)
zeros <- c(1, 0, rep(0, length(prob.fancy)))
zeros[2 + which(with(pfd1, V1 == 1 & V2 == 0 & V3 %in% 0:1))] <- -1
zeros[2 + which(with(pfd1, V1 == 1 & V2 == 1 & V3 %in% 0:1))] <- 1
zeros[2] <- 0
M <- rbind(M, zeros)


## other cases where we have a 1 - something
zeros <- c(1, 0, rep(0, length(prob.fancy)))
zeros[2 + which(with(pfd1, V1 == 0 & V2 == 0 & V3 %in% 0:1))] <- -1
zeros[2 + which(with(pfd1, V1 == 1 & V2 == 1 & V3 %in% 0:1))] <- -1
zeros[2] <- -1
M <- rbind(M, zeros)
zeros <- c(1, 0, rep(0, length(prob.fancy)))
zeros[2 + which(with(pfd1, V1 == 1 & V2 == 0 & V3 %in% 0:1))] <- -1
zeros[2 + which(with(pfd1, V1 == 0 & V2 == 1 & V3 %in% 0:1))] <- -1
zeros[2] <- -1
M <- rbind(M, zeros)
M[, -c(1:2)] <- M[, -c(1:2)] * -1

## find rows of Hrep that match M, then remove them

hremove <- which(colSums(apply(hrepd1$Hrep, MAR = 1, \(rr) apply(M, MAR = 1, \(dd) all(dd == rr)))) > 0)

hrep_to_text(hrepd1$Hrep[-hremove,], prob.fancy, sets1, simplify = TRUE)
```

Ok now we just need to do this automatically, and also remove the independence constraints from standard conditional independences that we treat separately.
